newsitem.title: UK: Med gas oil up on back of crude futures.
newsitem.headline: Med gas oil up on back of crude futures.

text.p: Med oil products were mixed on Tuesday, with gas oil and gasoline firming and fuel oil largely unchanged.
Gas oil firmed in line with stronger IPE futures, which closed $2.50 a tonne higher at $167.75 on front month July.
Spot differentials were unchanged with the market was mainly balanced and quiet. Russian 0.2 percent heating oil was assessed at cif high quotes +$2/$3 basis Genoa.

Attention is focussed on a tender by Greece for three cargoes of 0.2 percent sulphur heating oil, with one each for delivery in July, August and September. Turkey has tendered for three cargoes of gas oil, with the result due to be announced late on Friday.
Light ends gained $2 to $3 a tonne on Tuesday, tracking similar gains in Rotterdam and the U.S.
Gasoline rose to $194 cif Italy for premium unleaded, matching levels in Rotterdam. Naphtha rose to $174 cif Italy despite a closed arbitrage to the East which was keeping cargoes locked in Europe.
Dealers sid there had been minor problems with the quality of recent cargoes from Egypt. They expected those to be resolved over the next few days and saw steady exports from Algeria.
High sulphur was very quiet with only 35,000 to 40,000 tonnes of material said to be held by a major Italian refiner, with a price tag of some high fob Med plus $1.
Traders said the assessment of the market was hard until the fate of that cargo is known, and if any Russian material starts showing up in the region, some downward pressure may set into the market.
"Everyone is covered for the moment, so it all depends if Russian fuel starts coming into the Med, like in the north," one trader said.
